brief.tov:
Voice: a chess-literate friend with a point of view. Short opening line, concrete board detail,
confident explanation, restrained wit. Show the move or mechanism behind the headline.
Rules: no hype, no income or profit claims, no fake urgency, no invented numbers, testimonials or quotes.
At most 3 emoji, none as bullets. One idea, one CTA. Never copy a source's wording, structure or images;
rebuild the idea from our own position and explanation. Wager mentions always carry the adult disclosure
and are never paired with youth content. Name the move (SAN) and the square; give the reader something to try.

hook_templates.template: {number} {unit}. That is how long {player} thought about one move. The position:
hook_templates.note: Verify the number against the broadcast or the primary report.

hook_templates.template: {player} is the first to {verified record}. The idea behind it fits on one board.
hook_templates.note: Cite the source in the first reply.

ranked_formats.format: Record or first-ever claim with a number up front
ranked_formats.adaptation: Chess News, slot 2. A verified record, then one original lesson from the position that produced it. The number leads the first line.
ranked_formats.guardrail: Verify against a primary source before posting; never state a record you cannot cite.

ranked_formats.format: "This day in chess" history, birthdays and tributes
ranked_formats.adaptation: Chess Culture or News, slot 4 about twice a week. A dated fact plus the decisive position from that game. Our own copy.
ranked_formats.guardrail: Tributes after a death are not engagement material: use a plain, factual tone and no promotion beside them.

ranked_formats.adaptation: Chess News, slot 2. A short public quote (under about 15 words), exact and attributed, then our chess explanation of the position it refers to.
ranked_formats.guardrail: Quote accurately and briefly; no invented quotes; link the primary source.

avoid: Weekly "what to do this week" agenda posts
Medal lists and results tables as an engagement driver
Burst posting of four or more posts inside a day on one topic

brief.wager_disclosure: USDT matches are for adults (18+) where permitted. You can lose your stake.

output.extra_buttons: optional, at most one more CTA id

text: 9 days of club chess start on 16 October in Budva, Montenegro. The European Club Cup runs 16–24 October. A tip for following any team event: watch the match score, not only board one. The side that collects more points across all boards wins, and the quiet board often decides it. We will break down the key positions on the blog as they appear.
